i am writing to express my disappointment regarding the handling of an issue with my 2 year old samsung s22 ultra. after a recent firmware update, a green horizontal line appeared on my display, which samsung has officially acknowledged as a known issue with free replacements being offered. however, during my visit to the samsung service center last saturday, i was denied this free repair due to a minor dent on the edge of my phone. i also spoke with both the samsung helpline and the service center engineer, who stated that samsung's policy only offers free repairs for phones without physical damage, including minor dents. my question is when i purchased my phone two years ago for 1,10,000, was i informed that i would need a cover to avoid invalidating future repair eligibility? wear and tear on a 2 year old phone is normal, and i should not be penalized for a minor dent unrelated to the software issue. moreover, samsung did not provide any warning prior to the update that it could cause such display problems, particularly for phones with minor dents. it seems unfair that samsung established this policy after the green line issue became known. if the problem stems from samsung s firmware update, why is there discrimination between users with minor cosmetic damage and those without? while i am not an admirer of apple, i must acknowledge after purchasing the samsung galaxy s25 that the device falls short in terms of battery performance. this shortfall is largely attributable to samsung s emphasis on achieving a slim form factor, which results in a reduced battery capacity. consequently, the phone struggles to last a full day under moderate use, and the standby power drain is notably higher compared to that of the iphone. for context, i also use my employer issued iphone 15 alongside the s25, allowing me to compare their performance in daily usage scenarios. based on this direct comparison, i find the iphone 15 delivers superior battery life under similar conditions. my usage includes browsing, youtube, instagram, gas navigation, and regular phone calls, with no gaming involved. additionally, the galaxy s25 tends to exhibit heating issues during regular use a concern occasionally observed in the iphone as well, no complaints there. ultimately, my primary grievance centers on inadequate battery endurance. the trade off between slim design and battery capacity, which often necessitates carrying an external power bank, is unsatisfactory for my needs. i sincerely hope takes this feedback into account in future product designs.
topic_name: S25 vs S24 / iPhone Pro Max Comparison

the samsung galaxy s24 ultra and the newly announced galaxy s25 ultra both represent the pinnacle of samsung's smartphone offerings, but they come with several notable differences and improvements design and build s24 ultra known for its blocky design with sharp corners, it has a titanium frame and corning gorilla armor glass for durability. the s24 ultra had a reputation for its somewhat bulky feel due to its size and weight. s25 ultra this model introduces a more ergonomic design with slightly rounded corners for better grip and comfort, making it thinner and lighter than its predecessor. it retains the titanium frame but upgrades to corning gorilla armor 2, enhancing scratch resistance and reducing reflectivity. opinions some users appreciate the s25 ultra's shift to a more user friendly form factor, noting the ease of handling due to its reduced weight and dimensions. however, others might miss the more distinctive, business like look of the s24 ultra. display s24 ultra features a 6.8 inch dynamic ambled 2x display with a 120hz refresh rate, reaching up to 2,600 nits brightness. s25 ultra boasts a slightly larger 6.9 inch display with the same resolution, refresh rate, and brightness capabilities, but with narrower bezels for a more immersive viewing experience. opinions the larger, more bezel less display of the s25 ultra is generally seen as an upgrade, enhancing the visual experience without significantly increasing the phone's overall size. performance s24 ultra powered by the snapdragon 8 gen 3 for galaxy, it provided robust performance for its time. s25 ultra equipped with the newer snapdragon 8 elite for galaxy, promising even better performance, efficiency, and ai capabilities. opinions the performance upgrade is well received, with benchmarks showing significant improvements in both single core and mufti core scores, suggesting better efficiency and multitasking capabilities. camera s24 ultra already featured an impressive camera setup with a 200mp primary sensor, but the ultrawide was at 12mp. s25 ultra includes a new 50mp ultrawide camera, which should offer better detail in wide shots, alongside the same 200mp primary sensor. the s25 ultra also introduces new software features to enhance photography. opinions the camera upgrade, particularly the ultrawide, is a highlight for photography enthusiasts, offering clearer and more detailed images. however, some users argue that the s24 ultra's camera system was already top notch, questioning the need for an upgrade unless one values the macro capabilities of the new sensor. battery and charging both models maintain a 5000mah battery, but the s25 ultra benefits from more efficient hardware and software optimizations for potentially longer battery life. charging the s25 ultra introduces faster 25w wireless charging, although wired charging remains at 45w for both. opinions the lack of battery capacity increase in the s25 ultra has been a point of mild disappointment, but the efficiency gains from the new chipset are expected to mitigate this. the faster wireless charging is a welcome addition. general opinion upgrade justification for those with an s24 ultra, opinions are split on whether upgrading to the s25 ultra is necessary. the design and camera upgrades are significant, but the performance and battery life enhancements might not justify the cost for some. for new buyers the s25 ultra is generally seen as the better choice for those entering the samsung ecosystem or looking for the latest technology. in summary, the s25 ultra refines and slightly expands upon the features of the s24 ultra, offering a more comfortable design, enhanced camera capabilities, and better performance, which could sway users looking for the latest and greatest, but might not compel every s24 ultra owner to upgrade immediately.

comment_text: i ve been a loyal samsung user for years, proudly using the galaxy note 20 for the last five. it s been a reliable, powerful device that stood out especially with its unique design and premium feel. recently, i decided it was time to upgrade, so i visited a store to check out the new galaxy s25. to be honest, i was disappointed. the s25 s design feels like a departure from what made samsung special. it now has rounded edges and a lightweight frame that closely resembles the iphone so much so that it felt like a less premium imitation. it lacked the solid, luxurious feel i loved in previous samsung models. i asked if the s24 was still available, as it was the last version with the signature four corner design, but unfortunately, it's no longer in production. at that point, i made the decision to switch to the iphone 16 pro max. my reasoning was simple if the new samsung looks and feels like an iphone, why not just go for the original? what s more, samsung has removed features that once set it apart no more micros card slot and no included charger, just like apple did years ago. ironically, these were some of the reasons i had stopped using phones in the past. i really hope samsung reconsiders the direction they're heading in especially when it comes to design and camera performance. innovation and distinctiveness used to be the brand s strengths. as a long time fan, i genuinely hope to see those values return in future models.

just got my s25 in. its a learning curve, but still relatively familiar. one thing i do dislike though is the ostracization of google assistant. gemini is usable at best, and flubs a good chunk of the things i try to do with it, things that google assistant did with no complaints. gemini struggles with google home functions half of the time i try. when i ask it a simple question, its adds all of the ai fluff and extra information that i don't care or need to know about. if i ask for context or more information, i'd appreciate the extra effort it gives. unfortunately, it seems you can't use both at the same time. ideally, i could use the side button to activate google assistant, and have gemini tucked into the side bar should i need it. however, if i set it up as such, the side button will only work as google assistant until i try to launch the gemini ape, to which then the side button reverts to gemini. i would accept gemini being my side button if and only if my swipe up home button worked to pro google assistant i might still disable gemini lol . bixby wins, for once? it doesn't add the ai fluff junk that gemini does, and gives straight answers like google assistant. i love that it can work my phone, and something as simple as telling it to change my screen brightness, however easy that is for me, was a fun experience. doesn't replace google assistant for me though. 7 14 garbage move by samsung. hopefully i won't be reliant on anything galaxy ai related come 2026, as a subscription to use my phone is something i won't be paying for. if it was included with the guaranteed 7 years of updates, i'd understand, but releasing devices that are marketed with a service 25 series is all ai!!! , only to not provide said service not much later is enough to make me switch.
